data.description:
## Context
Live completion runs directly attribute 135-235 seconds to full ticket-store materialization. The store has about 5,500 ticket directories and 132,000 tracked files, so donor hardlinks avoid blob duplication but still perform work proportional to the whole inode tree. Evaluate a stable read-only completion environment that pins current tracker state cheaply while close, sidecar, and signature mutations continue against the normal live store.

## Plan
- Measure the cost and correctness of capturing the live tracker HEAD as an immutable read revision.
- Prove that a target ticket can be listed, extracted, and reduced from the pinned Git tree without materializing the whole store.
- In a disposable fixture, prove that subsequent live mutations do not alter pinned reads and remain visible to live reads.
- Compare scoped extraction time, file count, and bytes with known full-store materialization costs.
- Exercise final-validation mechanics for a ticket edit, a newly created child/query-result change, an unrelated ticket change, and a non-ancestor revision.
- Record implementation gotchas, performance risks, and a recommended boundary without modifying production code or documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Revision capture and pinned Git-tree reads have directly measured mechanics and cost.
- [ ] A scoped pinned ticket view reduces the same target state as the live store at the captured revision.
- [ ] A disposable mutation experiment proves pinned-read stability and live-write visibility.
- [ ] Scoped extraction time, file count, and bytes are compared with the measured full-store materialization path.
- [ ] Validation experiments distinguish relevant ticket/query changes from unrelated writes and fail closed for an incomparable revision.
- [ ] The ticket records evidence, gotchas, and the recommended design boundary.
- [ ] No production source, test, agent-guidance, or architecture-document files are changed.
data.title: Experiment with a pinned read-only ticket view for completion verification
